# Parley v0.1.58

This unnotarized test beta includes the fixes from an independent repository
review and two follow-up reviews. It strengthens agent permission boundaries,
worktree cleanup and recovery from failed persistence or stalled commands.

## Pane menu fix

- Move to Workspace stays stable while a pane is producing output or its
  metadata changes. The pane action menu keeps its choices and destinations
  for each opening, then refreshes them the next time it opens. This covers
  both the header ellipsis and the sidebar right-click/Control-click menu.
- The compact ellipsis button retains its existing pane actions and uses the
  same native menu handling as the toolbar.

## Permission and coordination fixes

- Agent permission roots now stay tied to the folder reviewed at launch.
  Terminal-reported folder changes cannot widen requested command runs, team
  folders or staged context, including when automatic command approval is on.
  Start, restart and resume retain the reviewed folder.
- Running panes retain their reviewed permission and Claude sandbox facts.
  Later profile edits cannot relax ticket requirements or hide writer warnings.
- Ticket verification checks the application-owned launch ancestry. Inactive
  pane credentials cannot recover tracked work, and legacy pane-token routes
  are removed from the native control socket.
- Requests use bounded, descriptor-based file reads. Overlapping deliveries
  to one pane are refused visibly, and callbacks from an old terminal cannot
  mark a replacement generation dead.

## Worktrees, history and command capture

- Git path handling preserves whitespace and line breaks across discovery,
  delegation snapshots and context/review capture.
- Cleanup refuses independent repositories inside ignored directories and
  preserves broken ownership records. Agent launch folders remain protected
  when a pane reports a different current folder.
- Failed context saves no longer publish an approval. Failed saves of an
  outcome that already occurred are visible in core health and retried.
- Retention changes cannot restore pruned history; partial failures are
  reported and can be retried.
- Command capture, cancellation and final waits are bounded, including when
  a descendant retains an output pipe. Permission disclosures match the
  session lifetime and the selected vendor's actual launch flags.

## Validation and release status

The menu regression check first reproduced 96 item mutations while the old
menu was open. The fixed menu remains unchanged across live updates, routes
selections to the displayed destination, and refreshes on reopening.

The preceding repository-hardening changes passed 399 native checks and 56
script tests in GitLab's macOS VM, plus the build and repository scans. The
menu fix is checked again by the complete release pipeline. Claude independently
reviewed the repository fixes and the final containment correction.

The GitLab release workflow runs the native checks and build again in its
macOS VM, then the soak, packaging and packaged-launch checks before publishing.
Its two Docker-only skips remain explicit because that VM has no Docker runtime.

This remains an ad-hoc-signed, unnotarized beta. A separate protected-tag
production preparation job is now available, but real Developer ID signing,
notarization and production update validation have not been exercised for
these changes. Follow the included installation instructions.
